newsitem.title: CANADA: German student charged with killing his father.
newsitem.headline: German student charged with killing his father.

text.p: A German university student was in custody on Thursday, charged with stabbing to death his father who had flown to Canada from Germany because he was alarmed about his son's mental health.
Krister Volkmann, 25, appeared in court on charges of second-degree murder on Thursday, looking panicked and confused.
"I am innocent and I don't even know exactly what I am charged with," a dishevelled Volkmann blurted out in the courtroom.
He was remanded in custody until Jan. 9 and the judge placed a publication ban on court proceedings.

Police said the man's father Helmuth Volkmann, 55, of Sprockhoevel, Germany, flew into Toronto on New Year's Eve after becoming worried by telephone calls from his son indicating he was suffering mental difficulties.
"Six hours later he was dead," said Metropolitan Police detective John Line.
The body of the elder Volkmann, a geography professor at Ruhr University in Germany, was found by police sprawled on the bedroom floor of his son's rooming house.
A German news agency report said Volkmann had travelled to Toronto to try and rescue his son from a cult, but police would not confirm a cult connection.
"There's nothing, absolutely nothing, at this point in time to suggest a cult. However ... we are continuing the investigation," Line told Reuters.
Krister Volkmann came to Toronto from Germany in August to further his post-graduate environmental studies at York University.
